identity.description: The Regent is a commanding royalty who wields two unique resources: Stars (a persistent secondary resource) and Forge (scaling damage for the Sovereign Blade). The Regent's playstyle is that of a strategist and commander — generating Stars to fuel powerful effects, building Forge stacks to make the Sovereign Blade devastatingly powerful, and managing dual resources for maximum efficiency.
identity.playstyle: Resource management and scaling. The Regent generates Stars through specific cards and abilities, then spends them to activate powerful effects. Simultaneously, Forge stacks accumulate to increase Sovereign Blade's damage. The Regent rewards careful resource planning — knowing when to generate Stars, when to spend them, and when to invest in Forge.
strengths: Dual resource system provides flexible, adaptive gameplay
Stars enable powerful effects that other characters can't access
Forge + Sovereign Blade scales damage to very high levels in long fights
Commander-style cards can buff allies or debuff enemies efficiently
Resource generation + spending creates satisfying engine-building gameplay
Stars and Forge both persist within combat, allowing for strategic planning across turns
weaknesses: Dual resource management adds complexity — mismanaging either resource hurts performance
Forge requires investment before Sovereign Blade becomes powerful
Stars spent are Stars gone — misspending Stars on low-impact effects is costly
Can be slow to start if Star generation and Forge building compete for card plays
Some fights end before Forge/Star engines come fully online
Balancing offense (Forge) and utility (Stars) requires experience

stars.description: Stars are the Regent's signature resource. Generated by specific cards and relics, Stars are a persistent secondary resource pool that persists across turns within a combat. Stars can be spent (consumed) to power up effects on other cards, or some effects may scale with the number of Stars you have without consuming them.
stars.generation: Stars are generated by playing specific Regent cards or triggering certain relics and effects.
stars.persistence: Stars persist across turns within a single combat but typically reset between combats.
stars.spending: Stars are consumed (spent) when playing cards that require Stars as an additional cost or that gain bonus effects by spending Stars.
stars.scaling: Some effects scale with the number of Stars you have, incentivizing Star accumulation before big spend turns.

forge_and_sovereign_blade.description: Forge is a stacking counter that increases the damage of Sovereign Blade. Each point of Forge adds damage to Sovereign Blade attacks. The Regent's primary damage scaling comes from building Forge and swinging the Sovereign Blade.
forge_and_sovereign_blade.forge_accumulation: Forge stacks are gained through specific Regent cards and effects. Forge persists within combat.
forge_and_sovereign_blade.sovereign_blade: Sovereign Blade is the Regent's signature weapon. Its damage is directly proportional to Forge stacks. More Forge = more devastating Sovereign Blade hits.
forge_and_sovereign_blade.scaling_curve: Forge provides linear scaling — each point of Forge adds consistent damage. In long fights, Forge can reach very high values.

star_engine.description: Focus on generating and spending Stars efficiently. Build a Star generation engine that produces Stars faster than you spend them, then use Star-powered effects for overwhelming advantage. The Star Engine archetype is about throughput — generate Stars and convert them into power.
core_strategy: Establish reliable Star generation early in each combat
Build Star reserves before spending — have enough Stars to power multiple effects
Identify high-impact Star spending effects in your deck
Balance Star generation cards and Star spending cards (aim for ~60% generation, ~40% spending)
Time your Star spending for maximum impact — save spending for critical turns
key_cards: Star generation cards — your engine's fuel source. Prioritize cards that generate Stars passively or as side effects
High-impact Star spending cards — effects that use Stars for powerful outcomes
Cards that generate Stars AND do something else (damage, block, draw) for efficiency
Star-scaling cards that grow stronger with more Stars accumulated
Cards that generate Stars at start of turn (passive generation)
strengths: Stars provide unique effects unavailable to other characters
Star engine can generate overwhelming advantage in long fights
Flexible — Stars can power offense, defense, or utility depending on the situation
Some Star effects don't consume Stars, rewarding Star accumulation
Passive Star generation (from Powers) provides value without card plays
weaknesses: Requires specific generation + spending cards — incomplete engine is weak
Star generation takes card plays that could be spent on damage or block
Spending Stars on the wrong effect is wasteful — recovery is slow
Early combat can be weak while building Star reserves

resource_management.generation_balance: Aim for 3-4 Star generation sources in your deck. Too few and you starve, too many and you waste card slots.
resource_management.spending_balance: Aim for 2-3 high-impact Star spending effects. Too many and you won't have enough Stars to fuel them all.
resource_management.timing: Generate Stars in the first 2-3 turns. Spend Stars on turns 3-5 for maximum impact. Continue generating for sustained fights.
resource_management.emergency_spending: Sometimes spending Stars for emergency block is correct even if it's not 'optimal' — survival trumps efficiency.

forge_sovereign_blade.description: Focus on building Forge stacks to make Sovereign Blade incredibly powerful. This is the Regent's primary damage scaling archetype — invest in Forge early, then deal devastating damage with each Sovereign Blade swing.
core_strategy: Build Forge stacks as quickly as possible in the first 2-3 turns
Play Sovereign Blade once Forge has reached a meaningful value (10+ Forge for good damage)
Cards that build Forge AND do something else (block, draw) are premium picks
In long fights, continue building Forge between Sovereign Blade swings for even more damage
Upgrade Forge generation cards for faster scaling
key_cards: Forge generation cards — your primary way to increase Sovereign Blade damage
Sovereign Blade — the damage payoff for Forge investment
Cards that play Sovereign Blade multiple times or reduce its cost
Cards that generate Forge as a side effect of other useful actions
Cards that multiply or double Forge stacks
strengths: Very high damage ceiling — Forge has no cap, so Sovereign Blade can deal enormous damage
Linear and predictable scaling — each Forge point is guaranteed value
Sovereign Blade + high Forge can one-shot or two-shot even bosses
Forge persists across turns — investment is never wasted within a combat
Simple to understand and execute compared to some other strategies
weaknesses: Forge does nothing without Sovereign Blade — if you don't draw Sovereign Blade, Forge is wasted
Forge investment takes turns that could be spent on damage or block
No defense inherent in the archetype — must pair with block cards or Stars for survival
Slow to start — Forge needs to reach meaningful values before Sovereign Blade is powerful
Fights that end quickly (2-3 turns) don't give Forge enough time to build

forge_targets.hallway_fights: 10-15 Forge is usually enough. Sovereign Blade with 10 Forge should handle most hallway enemies.
forge_targets.elite_fights: 20-30 Forge for strong Sovereign Blade hits. May need 2-3 Sovereign Blade plays.
forge_targets.boss_fights: 40+ Forge for devastating Sovereign Blade damage. Build aggressively in the first 4-5 turns.

balanced_regent.description: Balance Stars and Forge usage for a versatile strategy that adapts to any situation. Use Stars for utility and defense while using Forge for damage. The balanced approach doesn't commit fully to either resource, giving flexibility at the cost of peak power.
core_strategy: Generate both Stars and Forge simultaneously where possible
Use Stars primarily for defense and utility effects
Use Forge primarily for Sovereign Blade damage scaling
Adapt spending based on the specific fight — more defensive Stars against aggressive enemies, more Forge against tanky enemies
Don't commit too heavily to one resource at the expense of the other
strengths: Most adaptable Regent build — can handle any situation
Not dependent on any single card or combo
Balanced resource generation means you always have options
Can pivot to more offense or defense as the fight demands
Easier to build — doesn't require specific rare cards to function
weaknesses: Lower ceiling than pure Star Engine or pure Forge builds
Jack of all trades, master of none — may not have enough of either resource for peak effects
Can feel unfocused without clear priorities
Harder to evaluate card rewards — everything seems 'okay' but nothing is perfect

resource_balance_advice.description: Managing two resources (Stars and Forge) simultaneously is the core challenge of the Regent. Here's how to balance them.
general_principles: Generate resources you need FIRST, then spend them. Don't spend before you generate.
In short fights (hallway), focus on one resource — usually Forge for damage or Stars for utility
In long fights (elites, bosses), build both resources gradually over the first few turns
Don't hoard resources forever — spending them is how you generate value
Cards that generate BOTH Stars and Forge are premium picks — dual resource generation is extremely efficient

prioritize_forge: Against enemies with high HP (you need damage scaling to kill them efficiently)
When you have Sovereign Blade in hand or will draw it soon
When your Star spending options are limited or low impact
In fights where offense is more important than defense
prioritize_stars: Against aggressive enemies (you need Stars for defensive effects)
When you have powerful Star spending cards in hand
When Forge is already at a good level for Sovereign Blade
In multi-enemy fights where Stars-based utility effects are more valuable

common_resource_mistakes: Generating Stars without Star spending cards — wasted resource without a way to use it
Building Forge without Sovereign Blade access — Forge is useless without its payoff card
Spending all Stars early and having none for later turns — pace your spending
Ignoring one resource entirely — both Stars and Forge provide value, don't neglect either
Playing resource generation when you should be blocking or attacking — survival first

priorities: Understand which resource (Stars or Forge) your early cards support
Find direct damage cards for hallway fights — Sovereign Blade needs Forge time you don't have in short fights
Pick up Star generation to start building your resource engine
Get block cards — the Regent needs defense while setting up resources
Don't commit fully to Forge or Stars until you see what the game offers
Upgrade key resource generation cards for faster engine startup
act1.card_priorities: Direct damage > Star generation > Block > Forge generation
act1.elite_readiness: The Regent can handle Act 1 elites if you have some direct damage and block. Don't rely solely on Forge scaling for Act 1 elites — fights may be too short.
act1.boss_preparation: Ensure you have enough damage (Sovereign Blade + Forge, or direct damage) and block to handle a 6+ turn boss fight.

priorities: Solidify your archetype — Star Engine, Forge/Sovereign Blade, or Balanced
Add scaling that compounds over acts — Powers that generate resources passively
Improve block density for Act 2's harder enemies
Remove Strikes and Defends at shops
Upgrade resource generation and Sovereign Blade
act2.card_priorities: Scaling (Star or Forge) > Block > Card draw > Direct damage
act2.elite_readiness: Your resource engine should be functional. Use potions to cover setup turns.
act2.boss_preparation: Ensure your scaling is online and can handle high-HP boss fights.

priorities: Skip most card rewards — your deck is built
Prepare for the specific Act 3 boss
Ensure your engine can start fast enough for the final boss
act3.card_priorities: Only take cards that directly address a critical weakness.
act3.focus: Optimization. Upgrade your most impactful cards. Ensure your engine starts reliably.

common_pitfalls.resource_starvation: Not having enough Star generation sources means you can't fuel your Star-spending effects. Ensure you have 3-4 reliable Star generators.
common_pitfalls.forge_without_sovereign_blade: Building Forge is pointless if you can't draw Sovereign Blade reliably. Ensure you have Sovereign Blade access (or cards that create/find it) before investing in Forge.
common_pitfalls.overspending_stars: Don't spend all your Stars on turn 3 and have none left for turns 4-8. Pace your Star spending to maintain flexibility.
common_pitfalls.ignoring_defense: Resource building takes turns. If you spend 3 turns generating Stars and Forge without blocking, you might be dead before the engine comes online.
common_pitfalls.slow_engine_start: The Regent's engine needs 2-3 turns to start generating real value. Ensure you have enough block and early plays to survive the setup phase.
common_pitfalls.dual_resource_confusion: Don't try to build both Stars AND Forge at maximum speed simultaneously — you don't have enough card plays. Choose one to prioritize each fight based on the matchup.
common_pitfalls.hallway_fight_overkill: Don't build 30 Forge in a hallway fight against a 40 HP enemy. In short fights, play direct damage and finish quickly. Save the engine for elites and bosses.
common_pitfalls.sovereign_blade_timing: Don't play Sovereign Blade with only 3 Forge. Wait until Forge is at a meaningful value (10+) for the Sovereign Blade to be worth the card play.

unique_tips.star_budgeting: Think of Stars like a budget. Each turn, you 'earn' Stars from generation and 'spend' them on effects. Keep a positive balance until you're ready for a big spending turn.
unique_tips.forge_ramp_curve: Forge builds linearly. If you gain 5 Forge per turn, by turn 4 you have 20 Forge. That's usually enough for a devastating Sovereign Blade. Plan your Forge ramp and know when to swing.
unique_tips.adaptive_resource_use: In fights against aggressive enemies, spend Stars on defense. In fights against passive or tanky enemies, invest in Forge for faster kills. Adapt to each fight.
unique_tips.dual_generation_cards: Cards that generate both Stars and Forge are the most efficient cards in the Regent's kit. They should always be high priority picks.
unique_tips.sovereign_blade_scaling: Sovereign Blade is the Regent's version of Heavy Blade for Ironclad. It requires setup (Forge instead of Strength) but can deal comparable or higher damage.
unique_tips.star_spending_timing: The best time to spend Stars is when you have a clear advantage — Star spending effects often provide burst power that ends fights or turns the tide.

advanced_synergies_and_reworks.description: Grandmaster-level Regent knowledge: the Stars-vs-Forge rule, key card thresholds, and the Pale Blue Dot infinite.

never_mix_stars_and_forge.description: THE most important Regent rule. Stars decks and Forge decks should NEVER be mixed in the same run. The resources don't synergize, and split decks underperform either pure archetype.
never_mix_stars_and_forge.why: Stars cards consume Stars. Forge cards consume Forge. Cards that generate one resource don't generate the other. A 50/50 split deck has half-resourced cards across both engines and wins fewer fights than a pure 100% Stars or 100% Forge deck.
never_mix_stars_and_forge.decision_point: Commit to one archetype by mid-Act 1 based on what the game offers. If you see strong Star generators early, go Stars. If you see early Forge accumulators, go Forge. Don't try to hedge.

stars_archetype_s_tier.description: Stars persist across turns AND across combats, allowing massive stockpiling. Stars decks can support 25+ cards comfortably because cycle time matters less when you're patient.

key_cards.name: Big Bang
key_cards.effect: 0-cost. Generates Stars + cycles your deck efficiently.
key_cards.value: The Stars deck's bread-and-butter cantrip. Always take.

key_cards.name: Seven Stars
key_cards.value: Boss-killer finisher. The whole archetype builds toward this card.

key_cards.name: Pale Blue Dot
key_cards.effect: Power: the 5th card you play each turn is free — ignores both energy AND Star costs
key_cards.value: Breaks the entire resource limitation. Combine with massive Star-cost cards (Bombardment, Seven Stars) to bypass Star costs entirely. Effectively an infinite if you can reliably play 5+ cards per turn.

stars_archetype_s_tier.scaling_relics: Orbit (passive energy scaling — refunds 1 energy for every 4 energy spent). Compounds with Stars-deck's tendency to play many small cards.

forge_archetype_b_plus_tier.description: Sovereign Blade is a 'Retained' signature weapon ALWAYS in your hand. Forging at campfires permanently upgrades the blade's damage.

key_cards.name: Sovereign Blade
key_cards.effect: Permanent hand-card. Damage scales with Forge stacks. Forge bonuses persist across the run.

build_rules: Keep the deck EXTREMELY lean (under 20 cards) to ensure you have energy each turn to swing the blade
Prioritize Forge campfires over rest/upgrade (each Forge stack is permanent damage on every future Blade swing)
Remove Strikes/Defends aggressively — they don't help the Blade strategy
forge_archetype_b_plus_tier.anti_pattern: Forge builds get crushed by the reworked Doormaker (energy drain) unless you've maximized Sovereign Blade damage per swing. A 1-swing Blade boss-kill is doable; multi-card-per-turn Forge play is not.

heavenly_drill_threshold.the_rule: NEVER play Heavenly Drill below 4 Stars
heavenly_drill_threshold.the_math: The card pierces enemies by hitting X times. Above 4 Stars, the hit count DOUBLES. At 4 stars, it strikes 8 times for a base of 64 damage. At 3 stars, it strikes only 3 times for ~24 damage.
heavenly_drill_threshold.play_decision: If you have 3 stars and Heavenly Drill in hand, hold it. Generate one more Star (any source) and play it next turn for nearly 3x the damage.

minion_sacrifice_b_tier.description: Niche Japanese-meta build. Utilizes colorless cards to summon minions and instantly sacrifice them for burst value.
minion_sacrifice_b_tier.tier: B-tier — works in specific drafts, not a default plan
minion_sacrifice_b_tier.when_to_pivot: Only if you see multiple summon-sacrifice colorless cards in early shops/rewards

ripple_basin_synergy.effect: Grants block if you play NO attacks during your turn
ripple_basin_synergy.why_strong_for_regent: Regent often has turns where they ONLY generate Stars or pass to scale Sovereign Blade — no attacks played. Ripple Basin gives free block on those turns. Perfect synergy with the 'wait and stockpile' Stars playstyle.
ripple_basin_synergy.take_priority: Top-tier shop pickup for Regent. Often worth taking over a card.

doormaker_compatibility.description: Regent is one of the best Doormaker counters in the game.
doormaker_compatibility.why: Stars decks don't rely on net-positive energy per card. Forge decks play 1-2 cards per turn (Sovereign Blade + a draw card). Both archetypes naturally avoid the Doormaker energy drain.
doormaker_compatibility.build_for_doormaker: Either archetype works. Stars: focus on Pale Blue Dot. Forge: maximize per-swing damage so 1-2 swings end fights.
